newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Fed nixes study on power market competition.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed nixes study on power market competition.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve Board of Governors Friday turned down a request from a senator for a study on the potential economic impact of opening power markets to competition.

"In such matters, which involve relatively narrow sector-specific information, we tend to rely on analyses produced elsewhere," Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan said in a letter sent Friday to Senator Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).
Wyden last month asked Greenspan to submit a report by the end of February on the impact of deregulating power markets.

Citing lawmakers who have said that electricity market competition would increase economic growth by as much as $200 billion annually, Wyden asked Greenspan specific questions about power prices and equities market reaction to privatizing the federal power marketing agencies.
"Unfortunately, in this instance, it is questionable whether applying the resources we have in-house would yield the authoritative research you want," Greenspan replied.
Greenspan's letter steered Wyden to a study underway at the Energy Department and to academic research.
